title: useState basics
summary: useState stores component data that can change over time and trigger a re-render.
whenToUse: Use it for local UI data such as counters, selected tabs, form fields, toggles, and small component state.
do: Call useState at the top level of a component.
Use the setter function to update state.
Use a functional update when the next value depends on the previous value.
dont: Do not mutate state variables directly.
Do not call hooks inside conditions, loops, or nested functions.

codeSnippets.title: Practical counter example
codeSnippets.description: A small component that stores and updates local state.
codeSnippets.explanation: Clicking the button calls the setter, and React renders the component again with the new count.

commonMistake: Changing state variables directly instead of using the setter function.
interviewQuestion: What happens when you call a state setter?
interviewAnswer: React schedules an update and renders the component again with the new state value.

courseReference.notes: The project is a practical starting point for local UI state changes.

title: Event handlers
summary: Event handlers are functions React runs in response to user actions.
whenToUse: Use handlers for clicks, form changes, submits, keyboard events, and other user interactions.
do: Pass a function reference to event props.
Name handlers after the action they handle, like handleSubmit.
Keep handler logic short or move complex logic into helper functions.
dont: Do not call the handler while rendering unless you intentionally return another function.
Do not rely on stale state when the next value depends on the previous value.

codeSnippets.title: Handle a click
codeSnippets.description: Pass the handler function to the event prop.
codeSnippets.explanation: React stores the handler and calls it when the user clicks the button.

codeSnippets.title: Pass an argument
codeSnippets.description: Use an inline function when the handler needs a value.
codeSnippets.explanation: The arrow function waits for the click before calling onChoose with the selected value.

commonMistake: Calling the handler during render with onClick={handleClick()} instead of passing the function.
interviewQuestion: Why do we pass a function to onClick instead of calling it?
interviewAnswer: Passing a function lets React call it later when the event happens; calling it runs immediately during render.

courseReference.notes: Buttons and navigation actions are a compact way to practice event handlers.

title: Controlled inputs
summary: A controlled input gets its value from React state and updates that state on change.
whenToUse: Use controlled inputs when React needs to validate, submit, reset, or react to form values.
do: Store the input value in state.
Update that state in onChange.
Use the state value when submitting or validating the form.
dont: Do not pass value without an onChange handler unless the field is intentionally read-only.
Do not read directly from the DOM when React state already owns the form value.

codeSnippets.title: Controlled text input
codeSnippets.description: State is the source of truth for the input value.
codeSnippets.explanation: Every keystroke updates state, and the input displays the current state value.

codeSnippets.title: Use the value on submit
codeSnippets.description: Controlled state is ready to use when the form submits.
codeSnippets.explanation: The submit handler can use the latest state value without querying the DOM.

commonMistake: Providing a value prop without an onChange handler, which makes the input read-only.
interviewQuestion: What makes an input controlled in React?
interviewAnswer: Its displayed value comes from React state, and every change updates that state through an event handler.

courseReference.notes: Form fields are a practical place to connect input values to component state.

title: Form submit and preventDefault
summary: React form submit handlers receive an event object and usually call preventDefault to stop the browser page reload.
whenToUse: Use this pattern when a form should validate, create data, filter data, or call an API without leaving the current React page.
do: Handle submit on the form element.
Call event.preventDefault before running React submit logic.
Use controlled state values inside the submit handler.
dont: Do not put submit logic only on the button click when the form itself can submit.
Do not forget that pressing Enter in an input can submit the form.

codeSnippets.title: Handle form submit
codeSnippets.description: Stop the browser reload and use the controlled value.
codeSnippets.explanation: The form owns the submit event, preventDefault keeps React on the page, and query state contains the latest input value.

codeSnippets.title: Guard empty submissions
codeSnippets.explanation: The handler blocks empty input, sends clean data upward, and resets the controlled field after success.

commonMistake: Forgetting preventDefault, which makes the browser reload the page and resets React state.
interviewQuestion: Why do React form submit handlers often call event.preventDefault?
interviewAnswer: Because the browser's default form submit reloads or navigates the page, while React usually wants to handle the data in JavaScript.

courseReference.notes: The packing form submits controlled input data and then updates the item list.

title: Lifting state up
summary: Lifting state up means moving state to the closest parent that needs to coordinate multiple children.
whenToUse: Use it when sibling components need to read or update the same data, or when a parent must control which child view is active.
do: Place shared state in the closest common parent.
Pass the current value down as props.
Pass event handler functions down so children can request changes.
dont: Do not duplicate the same state in sibling components.
Do not let child components secretly own data that the parent needs to coordinate.

codeSnippets.title: Parent owns selected item
codeSnippets.description: A parent component owns the selected id and gives children data plus callbacks.
codeSnippets.explanation: The list and detail panel stay in sync because the selected id lives in their shared parent.

codeSnippets.title: Child requests parent update
codeSnippets.description: Children call a prop function instead of owning shared data themselves.
codeSnippets.explanation: The child handles the click, but the parent decides how selected state changes.

commonMistake: Keeping separate copies of shared state in multiple children, which makes the UI drift out of sync.
interviewQuestion: What does lifting state up mean in React?
interviewAnswer: It means moving shared state to the nearest common parent and passing values plus handlers down through props.

courseReference.notes: The app coordinates friend selection, add-friend visibility, and bill splitting from a parent component.

title: Derived state
summary: Derived state is data calculated from existing props or state during render instead of stored separately.
whenToUse: Use it for totals, percentages, filtered lists, selected objects, and display labels that can be recalculated from source data.
do: Calculate values from existing state when rendering.
Keep the original source of truth small and clear.
Use array methods like filter, map, and find for derived collections or values.
dont: Do not store a value in state if it can always be calculated from other state.
Do not update source state and derived state separately.

codeSnippets.title: Calculate a percentage from state
codeSnippets.description: A progress value can be calculated from the current list each render.
codeSnippets.explanation: Only tasks are state. completed and percent are derived from tasks, so they cannot get stale.

codeSnippets.title: Find selected data from an id
codeSnippets.description: Store the small stable id, then derive the full object.
codeSnippets.explanation: The selected object is recalculated from friends and selectedId instead of stored as a second source of truth.

commonMistake: Saving both the original data and a calculated version in state, then forgetting to keep them synchronized.
interviewQuestion: When should you avoid creating a new state variable?
interviewAnswer: Avoid new state when the value can be calculated from existing props or state during render.

courseReference.notes: The stats area calculates packed counts and percentages from the current item list.

title: Loading state
summary: Loading state tracks whether async work is currently in progress so the UI can show feedback.
whenToUse: Use it around API requests, form submits, lazy data loading, and any action where the user should not wonder if the app is stuck.
do: Set loading to true before async work starts.
Set loading back to false in finally so it runs after success or failure.
Use loading state to render a spinner, skeleton, or short status message.
dont: Do not leave loading true when an error happens.
Do not show stale results as if they are fresh while a new request is loading.

codeSnippets.title: Track request progress
codeSnippets.description: Use loading state to choose between a status message and normal UI.
codeSnippets.explanation: The UI shows loading feedback while the request is running and returns to normal after the request settles.

commonMistake: Setting loading to false only in the success path and forgetting the error path.
interviewQuestion: Why is loading state useful in React?
interviewAnswer: It lets the UI communicate that async work is in progress and prevents users from seeing a silent or confusing empty screen.

courseReference.notes: The app shows a loader while movie search results or movie details are being fetched.

title: Error state
summary: Error state stores a failure message or error object so the UI can explain what went wrong.
whenToUse: Use it when API calls, form submissions, parsing, or other async work can fail in a way the user should see.
do: Clear old errors before starting a new request.
Store a helpful message that the UI can render.
Render error UI separately from loading and success UI.
dont: Do not only log errors to the console.
Do not keep showing an old error after the next request succeeds.

codeSnippets.title: Show a request error
codeSnippets.description: Catch a failed request and render an error message.
codeSnippets.explanation: The component clears stale errors before retrying and shows a user-facing message when the request fails.

commonMistake: Catching an error but never storing it in state, leaving the user with no feedback.
interviewQuestion: How should a component handle API errors?
interviewAnswer: Catch the error, store a useful message in state, stop loading, and render a clear error state in the UI.

courseReference.notes: The movie search UI renders a specific error message when the API request fails or finds no movies.
